clue.text: Alceste's strange instrument, not used in Gluck's opera

definitions.text: instrument, not used in Gluck's opera

indicators.note: strange says the letters of the name are to be rearranged into something unfamiliar

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter; the heroine's name gives the seven letters to rework

explanation.surface: A remark that Alceste, Gluck's opera, uses an odd instrument absent from its own score.
explanation.walkthrough: Gluck's Alceste (1767) predates the celesta, invented in the 1880s, so the definition's tail is a factual flourish and the whole clue nearly reads as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard percussion instrument with metal bars, devised long after Gluck wrote.

clue.text: Army officer over three miles from comrade

indicators.note: over places the officer above the distance in this down entry

parts.note: Col is short for colonel
a league is an old measure of about three miles

explanation.surface: An officer travels a few miles away from a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the officer comes first; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a fellow worker, an associate in the same job.

clue.text: Behold a writer of verse — he makes a bit!

parts.note: lo is an old word for behold
a rimer, or rhymer, is a writer of verse

explanation.surface: Look at a poet, who produces a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' looks like 'a little'; it is the mouthpiece of a bridle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorimer is a craftsman who makes bits, spurs and other metal parts of horse harness.

clue.text: Comparatively loyal, he prevents bloodshed

explanation.surface: A more faithful man who stops people being hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch means steadfast, giving the comparative, and to staunch blood is to stem its flow from a wound.

clue.text: A rising service from a great distance

indicators.note: rising, in a down entry, means the service's letters are read upwards

parts.note: the RAF is one of the British armed services

explanation.surface: An air force climbing up from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'rising' means read from bottom to top, so the service reads upwards after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or from a long way off.

clue.text: Sugary confection uncle initially left his doting wife

parts.note: doting means fond

indicators.note: left says a letter departs from the word for the uncle's wife

parts.note: an uncle's wife is an aunt

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word uncle

explanation.surface: An uncle's fondly devoted wife is linked, oddly, with a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his wife' means the uncle's wife; 'left' takes away U, the first letter of 'uncle'. 'his' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugar paste used to make sweets and ice cakes.

clue.text: Its low-priced goods make an impression in the Navy

indicators.note: in says the impression sits inside the navy's word

parts.note: a fleet is a navy's ships
a mark is an impression left on something

explanation.surface: Cheap wares that catch the eye among sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue's picture of a cheap market; 'in' places the impression inside the navy word, and 'make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea market is a street market selling cheap second-hand goods.

clue.text: Comments followed by some players

explanation.surface: Remarks that some performers read from.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are brief written remarks, and musicians follow musical notes on a score.

clue.text: Obsequiously flatter University student during a tryst

indicators.note: during says the two letters come in the middle of the meeting

parts.note: a tryst is a date
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: Fawning over an academic who is on a romantic outing.
explanation.walkthrough: L, from the learner plate on British cars, is a stock crossword student.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to praise someone excessively, fawning over them.

clue.text: The wine is all right, though dropped in the river

indicators.note: dropped in says the letters fall into the river's name

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Wine is fine even after falling into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine.

clue.text: Immature creature associated with volcanoes, some say

indicators.note: some say means the word is as it sounds when spoken, in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: molten rock from volcanoes is lava

explanation.surface: A young animal somehow linked to volcanoes, according to some people.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech the R is silent, so the two words sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young, undeveloped form of an insect before it changes into an adult.

clue.text: Player surrounded by a crowd filled with wonder

indicators.note: surrounded by says the player sits inside the crowd's letters

parts.note: a ruck is a crowd or tussling mass of people
West is one of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: A performer mobbed by fans is overcome with amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge convention names players North, South, East and West; WEST goes between A and RUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck describes someone overwhelmed by amazement or reverence.

clue.text: Whose fur is this? Hesitant response

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
the reply to the question whose this is: it belongs to me

explanation.surface: Someone asked who owns a fur hesitantly claims it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'Whose fur is this?' sets up the reply 'Er, mine', which runs together as the fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter coat of the stoat, prized as a trimming for robes.

clue.text: One sent .to overthrow armies extremely swiftly

indicators.note: to overthrow armies is to throw their order over, so the letters are tumbled
extremely picks the first and last letters of the word swiftly

explanation.surface: An envoy is dispatched to rout armies with great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is ARMIES plus S and Y, the first and last letters of 'swiftly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a messenger or agent dispatched on a mission.

clue.text: Permits gin to be distributed in April, perhaps

indicators.note: distributed means spread about, so the letters of the two words are mixed

explanation.surface: Licences allow gin to be handed out in April.
explanation.definitionFit: April is one of the months of spring, an example of the season.

clue.text: No house painter required for this courtyard

indicators.note: No says the letters for house are to be left out of the painter's name

parts.note: William Hogarth was an English painter and satirist

explanation.surface: A courtyard that needs no decorator for any house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No house painter' looks like decorating advice; it is HOGARTH, the 18th-century English painter, without HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A garth is an enclosed quadrangle or yard, especially one inside a cloister.

clue.text: Manuscript identified by Church Army members to some degree?

indicators.note: identified by is a loose signal, helped by the question mark, that the church's people sit within the measure of degree

parts.note: in part means to some degree
the rank and file of an army are its men

explanation.surface: A document recognised by members of the Church Army, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church Army is a British Anglican evangelistic society, so the phrase looks like one unit, but it splits in two; 'identified by' is a loose insertion signal, softened by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Old manuscripts were written on parchment, prepared animal skin, so the material stands for the document.

clue.text: Own luggage-frame holding son's bag

parts.note: to own is to have

indicators.note: holding says the frame holds the letter inside

parts.note: a luggage rack holds bags
S is short for son; the 's adds nothing

explanation.surface: A personal luggage rack carrying a boy's bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A haversack is a canvas bag carried on the back or shoulder.

clue.text: Willingness to allow some variation

explanation.surface: Being prepared to permit a bit of difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is a readiness to put up with others, and in engineering the permitted margin of error in a measurement.

clue.text: Special knowledge… obtained once by one set free

parts.note: once means former, ex
per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: free says the letters of one and set are loosened into a new order

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Learning gained in the past by someone released from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set free' looks like a released prisoner; 'free' rearranges I and SET to give TISE. 'obtained' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is the skill or specialist understanding of someone trained in a field.

clue.text: Small boat taking many from the turret

indicators.note: taking ... from says the letter is removed from the turret's word

parts.note: a pinnacle is a small turret on a building
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number

explanation.surface: A dinghy carrying a crowd away from a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L, 'many' as the Roman 50, from PINNACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnace is a small boat carried on a larger ship.

clue.text: Watchfulness of Roman poet sacrificing rook

indicators.note: sacrificing, as in chess, means giving up the rook, so its letter is dropped

parts.note: Virgil was the Roman poet of the Aeneid
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: The alertness of an ancient poet who gives up a chess piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacrificing' is a chess term, fitting the rook.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of staying awake to keep watch.

clue.text: Fabulous creature making some angry phone-calls

indicators.note: making some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wonderful animal who rings people up furiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' looks like 'marvellous'; it means from fable.
explanation.definitionFit: The gryphon, or griffin, is a mythical beast with an eagle's head and a lion's body.

clue.text: Failure to employ lower-class man of learning

parts.note: non-U is British slang for not upper-class
a sage is a wise or learned man

explanation.surface: Not hiring a scholar of humble origins.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were 1950s British labels for upper-class and not upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonusage is the state of something not being put to use.

clue.text: Secluded places for cricket practice outside Gravesend

indicators.note: outside says the practice word goes round the letter

parts.note: cricketers practise in nets
the end of the word graves is its final letter

explanation.surface: Quiet spots for cricket training beyond a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravesend is a town in Kent, but here it splits as 'Graves end', the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a snug, secluded retreat.

clue.text: In a way, the container is barely sufficient

indicators.note: In says the container goes inside the way

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a can is a container

explanation.surface: In some respects, the box is only just big enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' looks like 'somewhat'; it puts CAN in ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means hardly enough, meagre.

clue.text: Earnest plea for proportional representation (always right)

parts.note: aye is a poetic word for always

explanation.surface: A heartfelt call for a fair voting system, made constantly and correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is a solemn request, usually addressed to God.

clue.text: A horse painter in Uttar Pradesh

parts.note: gee, as in gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse, written as its letter
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist on horseback in northern India.
explanation.walkthrough: RA means a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra, home of the Taj Mahal, is a city in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.

clue.text: Ages in RAF, moving around like sailors

indicators.note: moving around says the letters of the words are shifted about

explanation.surface: Years serving in the Royal Air Force, being posted about like naval men.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force; here it is just three letters of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafaring describes people who travel by sea or work as mariners.

clue.text: Made from wood, like a pen

parts.note: like means as
a pen is a female swan, and a female bird is a hen

explanation.surface: Something wooden, compared to a writing implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool; it is a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means made of the wood of the ash tree.

clue.text: Woman with articles to put in a case

parts.note: she refers to a woman
a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A woman with belongings packing them into a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a blade is to slide it into its scabbard or cover.

clue.text: Indirectly request free use of cane

parts.note: to request is to ask

indicators.note: free use of says the letters of cane are released into a new order

explanation.surface: Obliquely asking to be allowed a walking stick without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges CANE to ANCE; 'use of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to look sideways, obliquely or with suspicion.
